title: Size and layout of dwellings merit assessment criteria
text: M2.1.1 Dwellings have a primary living space that: i. is proportionate to the type and size of the dwelling and intended number of occupants; ii. has a physical and visual relationship with the primary garden area, private open space and/or public open space; and iii. incorporates environmental design principles, including passive solar design and appropriate daylighting and shading, appropriate for the climate. M2.1.2 Ceiling heights and room dimensions provide for well-proportioned spaces that facilitate good natural ventilation and daylighting. M2.1.3 The size and layout of a dwellings: i. is functional with the ability to flexibly accommodate furniture; ii. is appropriate to the intended number of occupants; and iii. ensures functional, high amenity spaces. M2.1.4 Development provides a mix of dwelling types, sizes and configurations that cater for diverse household types and changing community demographics, appropriate to the existing and/or future context of the locality. M2.1.5 Each dwelling provides adequate, conveniently located storage for large items that are: i. proportionate to the size of the dwelling and intended number of occupants; and ii. integrated into the design of the building and/or screened from view to ensure that it is not visually intrusive when viewed from the street. M2.1.6 The siting and layout of dwellings minimizes potential impacts on amenity and provide appropriate visual and acoustic privacy to habitable rooms by: i. locating, orienting or setting back habitable rooms; ii. providing adequate landscape screening as a buffer; and/or iii. providing acoustic treatments to reduce noise transfer.

replaces.note: Part C P2.1.1 to P2.1.6 wording carried

notes: from: ch3 M2.1. diverges: six merit clauses (Chapter 3 has three, with M2.1.2 printed twice); M2.1.2 to M2.1.4 are apartment-only. The M2.1.2 extract is interleaved ('good extent of natural ventilation'); text normalised.
